purpose: Determine whether investigations can safely share or merge case context without conflating different properties, dates, legal questions, evidence or answer states.
core_principle: MATCH IDENTITY AND SCOPE BEFORE MERGING; SHARED TOPIC ALONE IS NEVER SUFFICIENT.
merge_rules: Exact case identity may permit consolidation of duplicate investigation work.
Same property does not mean same investigation.
Same question does not mean same property.
Same property with different target dates remains distinct unless explicitly linked as related historical/current investigations.
Shared evidence may be linked without merging the cases.
Related subquestions may share evidence and case context while retaining separate answer states.
Different registration systems must not be silently merged.
Conflicting property identifiers block automatic merge.
Different material legal issues require separate subquestion or case states.
hard_stops: Never merge cases because they share an address string alone.
Never merge different target dates without preserving the distinct historical scopes.
Never merge different legal questions merely because they concern the same property.
Never use merged evidence to imply that the underlying cases have identical legal conclusions.
